Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health · documents: The v1 main text reports that 262 physicians created HealthBench tasks over eleven months, with practice experience in 60 countries and 26 specialties, and that all physician cohort members were compensated.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal18.healthbench.paper.compensated-physician-cohort

  • Original author-stage note: Actual new author-only source-content proposal. Distinct source-verifier/adversarial exact-digest reviews and coordinator admission are pending. No replication, independently adjudicated rights, commercial supplier credit, or deep credit is implied.
  • The appendix separately reports 268 physicians onboarded and describes later rotations and 31 removals. These source-stage counts are not fully reconciled in this packet; no final headcount is inferred by subtraction.
  • Compensation and cohort credentials are author-reported; payroll, licensing records, payment amounts and employer contracts were not independently verified.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health · documents: The v1 paper validates model grading against physician grades on the 34 predefined consensus criteria and selects GPT-4.1 as its default grader; it acknowledges that most example-specific criteria were written by individual physicians and were not validated by other physicians.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal18.healthbench.paper.grader-validation-scope

  • Original author-stage note: Actual new author-only source-content proposal. Distinct source-verifier/adversarial exact-digest reviews and coordinator admission are pending. No replication, independently adjudicated rights, commercial supplier credit, or deep credit is implied.
  • This reported validation scope does not establish perfect labels or independently verified agreement for every individualized rubric. No clinical safety conclusion or new grader run is added.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health · documents: The v1 paper grades each criterion as met or not met, applies its signed nonzero point weight from minus ten to ten, divides the sum by the available positive points per example, and clips the mean example score to zero through one.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal18.healthbench.paper.rubric-score-definition

  • Original author-stage note: Actual new author-only source-content proposal. Distinct source-verifier/adversarial exact-digest reviews and coordinator admission are pending. No replication, independently adjudicated rights, commercial supplier credit, or deep credit is implied.
  • This statement covers the overall scoring definition only. No implementation or numeric result was reproduced, and no conclusion about axis-level formula consistency is made.
